scope.purpose: Group frequently used controls for one area into a single tab stop with arrow-key navigation.
useCases: Formatting actions of an editor (IconButtons with Tooltips).
Actions on a table selection, with a More menu.
Display options of a view (a Popover of filters, a Menu of sort orders).
exclusions: Toggle buttons (pressed state) in v1: Button and IconButton have no pressed state (open question).
Text entry, Select or other arrow-key controls inside the toolbar in v1.
alternatives: ButtonGroup for a few independent actions, each a tab stop.
SegmentedControl or RadioGroup for a choice.

decisionsTaken: Like ButtonGroup, the toolbar has no surface and passes its size to every item, including Menu and Popover triggers and the controls inside Tooltips.
label is required: a toolbar is a composite widget whose purpose must be announced.
Roving focus shared with Tabs (lib/roving-focus): remembers the last focused item, arrows wrap, disabled items and separators skipped.
In a horizontal toolbar Down and Up Arrow on a Menu trigger still open its menu; in a vertical toolbar they move focus.
Items wrap onto further lines when they do not fit; no overflow menu in v1. (Superseded at round 3 by the overflow Menu.)
Separator child: a 1 px color.border.subtle line perpendicular to the orientation.

Gate question 3 resolved (user, 2026-11-09): the Tooltip skip and close delays become component tokens component.tooltip.skip-delay (300 ms) and component.tooltip.close-delay (100 ms) through a Tooltip Modify (rendering unchanged).
Gate question 4 resolved (user, 2026-11-09): the size a group imposes reaches Menu and Popover triggers; the same fix is applied to ButtonGroup, with a browser test in Toolbar and ButtonGroup.
Gate question 5 resolved (user, 2026-11-09): Toolbar v1 without toggle buttons; toggles later with a dedicated component or an IconButton pressed prop, on demand.
The toolbar size reaches its items through the ButtonGroup context key (ggb:button-group); Popover content resets it and Menu no longer does (gate question 4).

Roving focus from lib/roving-focus: keys handled in the capture phase and only when they come from an item, so that a Menu trigger in a vertical toolbar moves focus instead of opening, and keys inside an open menu or popover stay with it.

Round 2: the roving-focus module moved from src/lib into the Toolbar folder, Tabs using Bits UI Tabs; the shared rules (wrapping, Home and End, right-to-left, disabled items skipped) are checked by both browser suites.

Round 3: overflow Menu (More) instead of wrapping; moved units are hidden in place and offered as menu items built from their accessible name, icon and disabled state; choosing one clicks the original control. Menu and Popover triggers never move. A horizontal toolbar fills its inline size (otherwise the hidden items would feed back into its width).
